meta.title: DIP-I-496: show role and permission for a logged-in user
meta.prompt: Propose a design for this ticket: DIP-I-496

context.question: How does a logged-in user see which permission group they belong to, and where its guidelines are?
context.product: In Administration a permission group is a Group, and its name shows in the Users table, so an admin already sees who has what. A user can belong to more than one group, and a Steward group scopes its catalog access per catalog. The user never sees the group name, and some group names are technical, so the ticket asks for a separate display name set by an admin. The account menu in Explorer shows the avatar, the name, the email, Support and Logout.
context.gap: The account menu has no capture in app-context; its rows come from the attachment.

findings.claim: Account menus show the role as a secondary identity signal under the name, never above it.
findings.source: SaaS Permissions and Roles UX Patterns, SaaSUI Design

findings.claim: The menu shows the compact signal; a profile page holds the full breakdown of scopes.
findings.source: Managing roles and permissions, flow examples, Nicelydone

findings.claim: Multi-role products summarise the count and let the user drill in instead of listing every permission.

approaches.name: Role line
approaches.whatItIs: One plain text line under the email, showing the group's display name.
approaches.breaksWhen: A user in more than one group: one line cannot list several names without wrapping.

guidelines.text: Needs a click-through added to the badge

recommendation.summary: Ship the badges as the default under the name: for the many users who hold one group, that answers the ticket in the same glance as their email. When a user holds more than one group, or a group is scoped per catalog, the badge row becomes the way into the My access panel, so the detail exists when it is needed and never before.

reasons.title: It is simple where simple is correct
reasons.why: One group is the common case today. A badge costs one row and no interaction, so the common case does not pay for the rare one.

reasons.title: It does not break as the data changes
reasons.why: Groups are multi-valued and scoped per catalog. A plain text line has no room to grow into that; badges wrap and open into the panel.

reasons.title: It finishes the ticket's request
reasons.why: The ticket asks for a way to find the internal guidelines. The panel gives every group its link without cluttering the default view.

reasons.title: It reuses what exists
reasons.why: Badge and expandable row are existing kit patterns, so no new kind of component, and the change sits inside the current account menu.

change.adminSide: One optional Display name field on the create and edit group form, defaulting to the group name.
change.userSide: That display name, or names, surfaces as badges under the name in the account menu, opening into the My access panel when there is more than one.
